summary: In this story, a boy who is always the slowest runner on his school team learns pacing and steady breathing from his coach, and after weeks of practice, beats his own best time at the final school track meet.
introduce: Act out a short mime, such as checking your watch and tapping your foot, and ask students how you feel and how they know. Explain that in “Race to the Finish Line” they will use clues in the same way to work out what the writer does not say directly.

keyTerms.def: the speed at which someone moves or does something
a steady, repeated pattern of movement or sound
belonging to or about one particular person

challengeTerms.def: the ability to keep doing something difficult or tiring for a long time
a particular way of doing something that requires skill
continued effort to do or achieve something despite difficulties

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that beating your own best time matters more than winning a race? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain how Coach Ali's two tips helped Zaid improve.
struggling: Pre-teach pace, rhythm, and personal with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses endurance, technique, and perseverance to make an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
